title: Handout Technopreneurship - Prelim Reviewer
subject: Technopreneurship
coverage: Understanding Customers and Generating Effective Solutions
instructions: Select the best answer for each question.

questions.question: What best describes technopreneurship?

choices.A: A business approach built around technology and innovative technological products or services
choices.B: A business approach that avoids technology and focuses only on manual work
choices.C: A government program for regulating technology companies
choices.D: A business model limited to selling physical products locally

questions.answerText: A business approach built around technology and innovative technological products or services
questions.explanation: Technopreneurship combines technology and entrepreneurship to create, develop, and commercialize innovative technological products or services.

questions.question: According to the handout, when was the word technopreneurship first introduced?
questions.explanation: The handout states that the word technopreneurship was first introduced as early as 1987.

questions.question: When did technopreneurship gain significant momentum?

choices.B: During the 1950s

questions.answerText: During the early 2000s
questions.explanation: The early 2000s saw widespread Internet adoption and the rise of technology-driven ventures.

questions.question: Which is a core resource of technopreneurship?

choices.B: Digital tools, technical expertise, and innovation

questions.answerText: Digital tools, technical expertise, and innovation
questions.explanation: Technopreneurship depends heavily on digital tools, technical expertise, and innovation.

questions.question: What type of innovation is commonly associated with technopreneurship?

choices.B: Only minor changes to existing local products
choices.C: Innovation that avoids creating new markets
choices.D: Innovation based only on physical expansion

questions.answerText: Disruptive and technology-driven innovation
questions.explanation: The handout describes technopreneurial innovation as disruptive and technology-driven, often creating new markets or transforming industries.

questions.question: Why can technopreneurship scale rapidly?

choices.A: Because it depends only on local customers
choices.B: Because it requires many physical branches
choices.C: Because digital platforms provide global accessibility

questions.answerText: Because digital platforms provide global accessibility
questions.explanation: Digital platforms and global accessibility allow technopreneurial ventures to scale more rapidly than many traditional businesses.

questions.question: Why is the risk level of technopreneurship described as high?

choices.A: Because technology changes rapidly and markets can be uncertain
choices.B: Because it always operates in stable markets
choices.C: Because it does not use research or software

questions.answerText: Because technology changes rapidly and markets can be uncertain
questions.explanation: Rapid technological change and market uncertainty contribute to the higher risk level of technopreneurship.

questions.question: Which investment is more closely associated with technopreneurship?

choices.B: Only inventory and physical facilities

questions.answerText: Research, development, software, and technology
questions.explanation: Technopreneurial ventures commonly invest in research, development, software, and technology.

questions.question: What is FinTech?

choices.B: Digital tools and platforms that improve or automate financial services
choices.C: Biological systems used to create health products
choices.D: A type of physical retail store

questions.answerText: Digital tools and platforms that improve or automate financial services
questions.explanation: FinTech means Financial Technology and includes tools such as e-wallets, online banking, and digital payments.

questions.question: What is biotechnology according to the handout?

choices.A: The use of biological systems or organisms to develop products
choices.B: The use of social media to sell products
choices.C: The use of digital wallets for payments
choices.D: The use of cloud storage for accounting

questions.answerText: The use of biological systems or organisms to develop products
questions.explanation: Biotechnology uses biological systems or organisms to develop products for health, agriculture, and industry.

questions.question: What characterized entrepreneurship in the Pre-Industrial Era?

choices.A: Global digital platforms and cloud computing
choices.B: Local traders, merchants, artisans, and small producers

questions.answerText: Local traders, merchants, artisans, and small producers
questions.explanation: Pre-Industrial entrepreneurship was mostly local and involved traders, merchants, artisans, and small producers.

questions.question: Which development is associated with the Industrial Revolution?

choices.A: Steam engines, factories, and mass production
choices.B: Social media and cloud computing

questions.answerText: Steam engines, factories, and mass production
questions.explanation: The Industrial Revolution transformed entrepreneurship through technologies such as steam engines, factories, and mass production.

questions.question: What is an intrapreneur?

choices.A: An innovator working within a company
choices.B: A customer who buys from several stores
choices.C: A government official who manages startups

questions.answerText: An innovator working within a company
questions.explanation: Intrapreneurs are innovators who work within established companies.

questions.question: Which period saw computers, the Internet, and telecommunications reshape business models?

choices.B: Industrial Revolution
choices.C: Late 20th Century Information Age and Globalization

questions.answerText: Late 20th Century Information Age and Globalization
questions.explanation: The late 20th century Information Age and Globalization expanded access to global markets, digital tools, and faster communication.

questions.question: Which technopreneur is associated with PayMaya (Maya) and Voyager Innovations?

choices.B: Orlando B. Vea

questions.answerText: Orlando B. Vea
questions.explanation: Orlando B. Vea is listed with PayMaya (Maya) and Voyager Innovations in fintech and digital payments.

questions.question: Which venture is associated with Cholo Tagaysay?

choices.B: Coins.ph

questions.answerText: KonsultaMD
questions.explanation: Cholo Tagaysay is associated with KonsultaMD in health-tech and telemedicine.

questions.question: Which technopreneur is associated with the AI-driven recruitment platform Kalibrr?

choices.B: Paul Rivera

questions.answerText: Paul Rivera
questions.explanation: Paul Rivera developed Kalibrr, an AI-driven recruitment platform used across Southeast Asia.

questions.topic: Technology as a Driver of Innovation
questions.question: How does technology improve efficiency and quality?

choices.A: By making processes slower and more manual
choices.B: By making processes faster, more accurate, and more consistent
choices.C: By removing access to digital systems

questions.answerText: By making processes faster, more accurate, and more consistent
questions.explanation: Technology-driven innovations improve speed, accuracy, and consistency in business processes.

questions.question: Which emerging technology is described as enabling secure digital transactions and smart contracts?

choices.B: Virtual Reality

questions.answerText: Blockchain
questions.explanation: The handout states that blockchain can enable secure digital transactions and smart contracts.

questions.question: Which trait means being willing to experiment and invest in new ideas while using data to reduce risk?

choices.B: Opportunity-Oriented

questions.answerText: Risk-Taking with Analysis
questions.explanation: Risk-Taking with Analysis combines willingness to experiment with data-based efforts to minimize risk.

questions.question: What does a macro view focus on?

choices.B: Large-scale forces affecting industries, economies, and societies
choices.C: Only the internal layout of one company

questions.answerText: Large-scale forces affecting industries, economies, and societies
questions.explanation: A macro view examines broad trends and large-scale forces instead of focusing only on a single company or product.

questions.question: A shortage of electric vehicle charging stations is an example of which macro category?

choices.B: Social Developments

questions.answerText: Industry Trends & Challenges
questions.explanation: The handout uses the shortage of EV charging stations as an example of an industry trend or challenge.

questions.question: Public health failures during COVID-19 are used as an example of which macro category?

choices.B: Social Developments

questions.answerText: Social Developments
questions.explanation: Public health failures during COVID-19 are listed under Social Developments.

questions.question: Ethical challenges in Artificial Intelligence are an example of which macro category?

choices.B: Social Developments

questions.answerText: Technological Advancements
questions.explanation: The handout places ethical challenges in AI under Technological Advancements.

questions.question: Rising demand for freelance platforms due to increased reliance on independent professionals is an example of what?

choices.B: Social Jobs

questions.answerText: Economic Forces
questions.explanation: The handout identifies increased reliance on independent professionals and demand for freelance platforms as an economic force.

questions.question: Which is a possible risk of ignoring the macro environment?

choices.A: Building outdated products for shrinking markets
choices.B: Automatically finding more investors

questions.answerText: Building outdated products for shrinking markets
questions.explanation: Ignoring economic, social, and technological trends can lead to outdated products and wasted resources.

questions.question: Which is a benefit of adopting a macro perspective?

choices.B: Anticipating change and developing proactive strategies

questions.answerText: Anticipating change and developing proactive strategies
questions.explanation: Macro analysis helps technopreneurs anticipate change instead of only reacting to it.

questions.question: How can a macro perspective help an aspiring technopreneur attract investors?

choices.A: By avoiding discussion of market trends
choices.B: By showing awareness of large-scale trends and future market potential
choices.C: By focusing only on a single internal process
choices.D: By refusing to adapt to technological shifts

questions.answerText: By showing awareness of large-scale trends and future market potential
questions.explanation: Investors are more likely to fund ventures that demonstrate awareness of large-scale trends and future potential.

questions.question: What does macro analysis mean in the 'Genius of the AND'?

choices.A: Zooming out to broad trends, global forces, and future landscapes
choices.B: Zooming in only on exact customer pain points
choices.D: Focusing only on one product feature

questions.answerText: Zooming out to broad trends, global forces, and future landscapes
questions.explanation: Macro analysis zooms out to identify broad market opportunities, societal shifts, technological disruptions, and long-term risks.

questions.question: What does micro analysis focus on?

choices.A: Specific customers, operational details, and exact pain points
choices.B: Only international policies

questions.answerText: Specific customers, operational details, and exact pain points
questions.explanation: Micro analysis zooms in on specific customers, operations, and precise pain points.

questions.question: Which is an example of a micro-level initiative?

choices.B: Tree planting activities

questions.answerText: Tree planting activities
questions.explanation: Tree planting is listed as a local or personal micro-level initiative.

questions.question: Which is an example of a super-macro initiative?

choices.A: Using an energy-efficient appliance at home
choices.B: Reducing single-use plastics personally
choices.C: The Paris Agreement and emissions goals

questions.answerText: The Paris Agreement and emissions goals
questions.explanation: Global agreements such as the Paris Agreement are examples of super-macro policies and initiatives.

questions.question: What is a problem space?

choices.A: Only the technical solution a team wants to build
choices.B: The complete context of a problem, including people, environment, and influencing factors
choices.C: A list of product features only

questions.answerText: The complete context of a problem, including people, environment, and influencing factors
questions.explanation: A problem space includes the problem itself, the people affected, the environment, and relevant constraints or factors.

questions.question: Which is NOT one of the four main components of a problem space in the handout?

choices.B: The People

questions.answerText: The Advertising Budget
questions.explanation: The four components are the Problem, the People, the Environment, and Constraints & Factors.

questions.question: Which statement best describes a market in the handout?

choices.B: People or companies that share a need, may pay for a solution, and experience the problem
choices.C: Only people who already own a startup
choices.D: Only companies located in one city

questions.answerText: People or companies that share a need, may pay for a solution, and experience the problem
questions.explanation: A market consists of people or companies with a similar need or problem, willingness to pay, and meaningful experience of that problem.

questions.question: What does problem-first thinking focus on?

choices.A: Building something interesting even without demand
choices.B: Solving a real and persistent problem
choices.C: Choosing a technology before identifying users
choices.D: Adding as many features as possible

questions.answerText: Solving a real and persistent problem
questions.explanation: Problem-first thinking starts with a real, persistent problem instead of starting with a preferred idea or feature.

questions.question: What makes a problem validated?

choices.A: It affects a clear group of people frequently and significantly
choices.B: The founder personally likes the idea

questions.answerText: It affects a clear group of people frequently and significantly
questions.explanation: A validated problem affects a clear group of people and happens often enough or severely enough to matter.

questions.question: How can a team validate a proposed solution?

choices.A: Avoid users until the product is finished
choices.B: Ask users, create prototypes, and evaluate demand
choices.C: Rely only on the founder's opinion

questions.answerText: Ask users, create prototypes, and evaluate demand
questions.explanation: Solution validation involves testing feasibility and desirability through users, prototypes, and demand evaluation.

questions.question: What is confirmation bias in problem analysis?

choices.A: Forcing a preferred solution to fit a problem even when it may not solve it
choices.B: Exploring many possible explanations
choices.D: Changing a solution after valid evidence

questions.answerText: Forcing a preferred solution to fit a problem even when it may not solve it
questions.explanation: Confirmation bias occurs when innovators force a solution they already like to fit the problem.

questions.question: What is tunnel vision?

choices.B: Becoming overly focused on one idea and ignoring better possibilities

questions.answerText: Becoming overly focused on one idea and ignoring better possibilities
questions.explanation: Tunnel vision means focusing too narrowly on one idea and failing to consider better alternatives.

questions.question: Which quality helps innovators understand a problem through the eyes of users?

choices.B: Tunnel Vision

questions.answerText: Empathy
questions.explanation: Empathy helps innovators understand users' pain points, frustrations, and emotions.

questions.question: What is the difference between symptoms and root causes?

choices.A: Symptoms are underlying reasons, while root causes are surface-level issues
choices.B: Symptoms are surface-level issues, while root causes are underlying reasons
choices.C: They always mean the same thing
choices.D: Root causes are always customer features

questions.answerText: Symptoms are surface-level issues, while root causes are underlying reasons
questions.explanation: The handout explains that treating symptoms gives temporary fixes, while addressing root causes supports long-term solutions.

questions.question: Who developed the 5 Whys technique?

choices.B: Steve Jobs

questions.answerText: Sakichi Toyoda
questions.explanation: The handout credits Sakichi Toyoda, founder of Toyota, with developing the 5 Whys technique.

questions.question: In the handout's 'late for morning classes' example, what root cause was identified after applying the 5 Whys?

choices.B: A lack of discipline and a structured daily routine

questions.answerText: A lack of discipline and a structured daily routine
questions.explanation: The example identifies lack of discipline and the absence of a structured daily routine as the root cause.

questions.question: Which problem is specifically mentioned as being addressed by EdTech startups such as BYJU's, Unacademy, and Khan Academy?

choices.A: Limited access to high-quality teachers and personalized instruction
choices.B: Lack of electric vehicle charging stations

questions.answerText: Limited access to high-quality teachers and personalized instruction
questions.explanation: The EdTech example highlights limited access to quality teachers, low engagement, stressful exam preparation, and lack of personalized instruction.

questions.question: What is a customer segment?

choices.A: A random set of people with unrelated needs
choices.B: A clearly defined group sharing similar needs, preferences, behaviors, or characteristics
choices.C: Only the employees of a company
choices.D: Only customers who buy the most expensive product

questions.answerText: A clearly defined group sharing similar needs, preferences, behaviors, or characteristics
questions.explanation: Customer segments group individuals or organizations with similar needs, preferences, behaviors, or characteristics.

questions.question: Why is customer segmentation especially important in technopreneurship?

choices.A: Technology solutions often target specific pain points and user behaviors
choices.B: Technology products should always target everyone
choices.C: Segmentation removes the need for customer research

questions.answerText: Technology solutions often target specific pain points and user behaviors
questions.explanation: Well-defined segments help technopreneurs build apps, platforms, and services around real pain points and digital behaviors.

questions.question: What is one reason startups segment customers?

choices.A: To make every user receive the exact same experience
choices.B: To understand customer needs more deeply

questions.answerText: To understand customer needs more deeply
questions.explanation: Segmentation reveals patterns in motivations, frustrations, buying behaviors, and routines.

questions.question: Why is segmentation useful when developing a Minimum Viable Product (MVP)?

choices.A: An MVP should focus on a specific group rather than everyone
choices.B: An MVP should include every possible feature for every customer
choices.C: Segmentation prevents startups from testing products
choices.D: Segmentation removes the need for pricing decisions

questions.answerText: An MVP should focus on a specific group rather than everyone
questions.explanation: The handout states that startups should focus the MVP on a specific segment rather than trying to serve everyone.

questions.question: According to the handout, what percentage of failed startups attributed failure to 'no market need'?
questions.explanation: The handout states that 42% of failed startups attributed their failure to no market need.

questions.question: Which failure factor is listed at 29% in the handout?

choices.B: Pricing and cost issues

questions.answerText: Running out of cash
questions.explanation: The handout lists running out of cash at 29% of failures.

questions.question: What does B2C mean?

choices.A: Business selling directly to individual customers
choices.B: Business selling only to government agencies
choices.C: Business selling only to other businesses
choices.D: Customer selling only to another customer

questions.answerText: Business selling directly to individual customers
questions.explanation: Business-to-Consumer (B2C) refers to businesses selling products or services directly to individual customers.

questions.question: Which is an example of a B2B offering in the handout?

choices.B: A personal streaming subscription
choices.C: A grocery delivery order for one household
choices.D: A mobile wallet used by one consumer

questions.answerText: SaaS platforms
questions.explanation: SaaS platforms are listed as examples of Business-to-Business offerings.

questions.question: Which is an example of Business-to-Government (B2G)?

choices.B: A movie streaming subscription
choices.D: A shoe purchase from an online store

questions.answerText: IT infrastructure for LGUs
questions.explanation: B2G includes products and services sold to government agencies or public institutions, such as IT infrastructure for LGUs.

questions.question: What is the main difference between a buyer and a user?

choices.A: The buyer pays, while the user actually uses the product
choices.B: The buyer always uses the product, while the user always pays
choices.C: The buyer and user can never be the same person

questions.answerText: The buyer pays, while the user actually uses the product
questions.explanation: A buyer is the one who pays, while a user is the one who actually uses the product; sometimes they are the same person and sometimes they are not.

questions.question: Which segmentation method is based on age, gender, income, education, and occupation?

choices.B: Psychographic segmentation

questions.answerText: Demographic segmentation
questions.explanation: Demographic segmentation groups customers using characteristics such as age, gender, income, education, and occupation.

questions.question: Which segmentation method is based on lifestyles, attitudes, values, and interests?

choices.B: Behavioral segmentation

questions.answerText: Psychographic segmentation
questions.explanation: Psychographic segmentation focuses on lifestyles, attitudes, values, and interests.

questions.question: Which segmentation method is based on usage frequency, habits, spending patterns, and loyalty?

choices.B: Demographic segmentation

questions.answerText: Behavioral segmentation
questions.explanation: Behavioral segmentation is based on usage, habits, spending patterns, and loyalty.

questions.question: What is the main idea of Jobs-To-Be-Done (JTBD)?

choices.A: Customers hire products to accomplish a job
choices.B: Customers buy products only because of technical specifications
choices.C: Customers do not care about outcomes
choices.D: Customers should always choose the cheapest option

questions.answerText: Customers hire products to accomplish a job
questions.explanation: JTBD focuses on the idea that customers choose or 'hire' products to accomplish specific goals.

questions.question: Which JTBD component describes the task or goal a user wants to accomplish?

choices.B: Emotional Job

questions.answerText: Functional Job
questions.explanation: Functional Jobs are the tasks or goals users want to accomplish.

questions.question: Which JTBD component describes how a user wants to feel during or after using a product?

choices.B: Emotional Job

questions.answerText: Emotional Job
questions.explanation: Emotional Jobs describe how the user wants to feel during or after using a solution.

questions.question: Which JTBD component describes how a user wants to be perceived by other people?

choices.B: Emotional Job

questions.answerText: Social Job
questions.explanation: Social Jobs focus on how users want others to perceive them.

questions.question: Why should technopreneurs communicate benefits instead of only features?

choices.A: Customers care about the outcomes a product helps them achieve
choices.B: Features are always useless
choices.C: Benefits remove the need for a working product
choices.D: Customers only care about technical terms

questions.answerText: Customers care about the outcomes a product helps them achieve
questions.explanation: From the JTBD perspective, customers care about what a product enables them to accomplish, not just its features.

questions.question: What is a customer persona?

choices.A: A semi-fictional representation of a target customer based on research-related characteristics
choices.B: A completely imaginary customer with no connection to research

questions.answerText: A semi-fictional representation of a target customer based on research-related characteristics
questions.explanation: A persona represents a target customer using factors such as demographics, psychographics, goals, pain points, JTBD, and behavior patterns.

questions.question: How can personas support product development?

choices.A: They provide a reference point for deciding whether features would help target users
choices.B: They eliminate the need to understand customers
choices.C: They guarantee every feature will succeed
choices.D: They are used only for accounting

questions.answerText: They provide a reference point for deciding whether features would help target users
questions.explanation: Teams can compare proposed features against persona goals, habits, motivations, and challenges.

questions.question: What is customer validation?

choices.A: Testing assumptions about customer problems, needs, and behaviors through real-world interactions
choices.B: Writing code before speaking to any customers
choices.C: Choosing a target market only from personal opinion
choices.D: Launching a final product without testing

questions.answerText: Testing assumptions about customer problems, needs, and behaviors through real-world interactions
questions.explanation: Customer validation tests assumptions using direct interactions such as interviews, surveys, and prototype testing.

questions.question: What is the first step in the handout's scientific approach to customer validation?

choices.B: Scale the business

questions.answerText: Create a hypothesis
questions.explanation: The process begins by defining assumptions about the problem, target customers, or solution.

questions.question: Which is one of the four essential areas startups must validate?

choices.B: Office Decoration

questions.answerText: Team Capability
questions.explanation: The four areas are customer problems/needs, product or service feasibility, team capability, and economic sustainability.

questions.question: Why are customer interviews considered a core validation method?

choices.A: They provide qualitative insights into customer context and lived experiences
choices.B: They replace the need to listen to users

questions.answerText: They provide qualitative insights into customer context and lived experiences
questions.explanation: Interviews help founders learn directly from users and capture deeper qualitative insights that surveys may miss.

questions.question: Which question style is recommended during customer interviews?

choices.B: Leading questions designed to influence answers

questions.answerText: Open-ended questions
questions.explanation: The handout recommends open-ended questions, active listening, empathy, and deeper follow-up questions.

questions.question: What does Customer Problem Fit measure?

choices.A: How well a startup's idea aligns with real customer needs
choices.B: How many employees a startup has

questions.answerText: How well a startup's idea aligns with real customer needs
questions.explanation: Customer Problem Fit checks whether the identified problem matches real customer challenges and whether the proposed direction fits their routines and needs.

questions.question: Which framework is described as human-centered and empathy-first?

choices.B: Lean Startup

questions.answerText: Design Thinking
questions.explanation: Design Thinking emphasizes deeply understanding user needs and iterative prototyping.

questions.question: Which framework is based on the build, measure, and learn cycle?

choices.B: Lean Startup

questions.answerText: Lean Startup
questions.explanation: Lean Startup uses the build-measure-learn cycle for early and continuous validation.

questions.question: What should a startup do when interviews strongly validate the problem, persona, and JTBD?

choices.B: Pivot

questions.answerText: Persist
questions.explanation: Persisting is appropriate when interviews strongly validate the current problem, persona, and job-to-be-done.

questions.question: When is a pivot most appropriate?

choices.A: When the problem is weak, unclear, or misaligned with customer needs
choices.B: When the problem, persona, and JTBD are strongly validated
choices.C: When only minor adjustments are needed
choices.D: Whenever one interviewee gives positive feedback

questions.answerText: When the problem is weak, unclear, or misaligned with customer needs
questions.explanation: A pivot is appropriate when validation shows low urgency, segment mismatch, strong existing alternatives, or more pressing customer needs elsewhere.
